newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Europe's big companies asked to help the small ones.
newsitem.headline: Europe's big companies asked to help the small ones.

text.p: Europe's ability to create jobs and compete on world markets would improve if big companies worked more closely with small ones, a group of top European corporations said Monday.

The heavyweights should, for example, forge close business links with small firms, consider spinning off units to them and share training resources, said a report by the European Round Table of Industrialists (ERT).

"Partnerships between large and small companies have become a central feature of the business world," said Morris Tabaksblat, chairman and CEO of Anglo-Dutch conglomerate Unilever Plc, addressing an ERT luncheon.
"Europe is losing out in comparison to its competitors," he said. "It is not modernising its industrial and economic structures quickly enough."
The round table's members are the chairmen of 45 leading European companies.
The report found that small and medium-sized enterprises that received support from large companies had an 80 percent survival rate after five years -- compared with the 50 percent European average.
Governments could help by easing up on the regulatory burdens that hamper small and medium-sized enterprises, "one of Europe's major competitive handicaps," it added.
